In a plane, 'is skein-aligned to' follow.why: A made-up relation (skein_aligned_to, fictional, no property tags before the insert) given a property and applied to real instances. The name "skein-aligned" is not a mathematical term, so a model has no default reading of it with this property, and an unrecorded relation has no property to contradict. Paired with mathematics-replace-0017.

notes: RBox expansion, role chain, paired with mathematics-replace-0017 (which removes the chain 'is perpendicular to' followed by 'is parallel to' gives 'is perpendicular to'). Here a made-up relation between lines is composed with the real 'is parallel to', which the models must hold: both instances leave the real hop (the y-axis is parallel to the lines x = 5 and x = 9) out of the prompt, so the answer needs the stored bridge plus the inserted chain (hops 2). The vertical lines are Wikipedia's own description (a vertical line is a line parallel to the y-axis). Every original answer is null. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: the first instance asks whether the conclusion follows (yes), the second whether it could fail (no); the cross-lingual queries ask the first instance. The propositional negation is worded 'Is it true that in a plane ... does not give ...?'. Side facts (82 even, 23 even) are copied from the paired revision. Near unrelated asks a different composition of real relations whose answer is no ('is parallel to' followed by 'is perpendicular to' gives 'is perpendicular to', not 'is parallel to'); a leak that makes every composition yield its first relation would turn it to yes.
